title: Bug: PiAgent missing from Synchronizer.parseSkills switch
description: The switch in internal/sync/sync.go:217 enumerates 6 platforms but omits model.PiAgent. Result: any sync where the source is 'pi-agent' fails with 'unsupported platform: pi-agent', even though tiered.NewForPlatform, validation.GetPlatformPath, and the transformer all handle it. Add the missing case using piagent.New(basePath).
acceptance_criteria: case model.PiAgent: p = piagent.New(basePath) added; new e2e test sync pi-agent -> claudecode passes
close_reason: Added case model.PiAgent to parseSkills switch in sync.go with piagent.New(basePath); added TestSynchronizer_Sync_PiAgentToClaudeCode e2e test; all 27 packages pass

title: Epic: Provider coverage parity across all 7 platforms
description: The codebase has parsers for ClaudeCode, Cursor, Codex, PiAgent, Copilot, Gemini, and PiDev — but Copilot/Gemini/PiDev are still treated as 'reference-only' in docs and lack e2e coverage. This epic tracks closing the gap between code reality and the user-facing surface (docs, help text, tests, transformer fidelity) so all 7 platforms reach implemented-tier parity.

title: Update README.md: add all 7 platforms, correct Go version, complete env-var list
description:
README currently only advertises Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex — 4 of 7 supported platforms (PiAgent, Copilot, Gemini, Pi.dev) are missing from the headline and features list. The 'Requirements' section says Go 1.25.4 while go.mod line 3 now reads go 1.26.1. The env-var override table lists only 3 of 7 platform overrides; the SKILLSYNC_COPILOT_SKILLS_PATHS, SKILLSYNC_GEMINI_SKILLS_PATHS, SKILLSYNC_PIAGENT_SKILLS_PATHS, SKILLSYNC_PIDEV_SKILLS_PATHS vars are undocumented.

Files: README.md lines 1-10, 60-80; go.mod line 3.

Acceptance: README headline lists all 7 platforms; Go version matches go.mod; env-var override section enumerates all 7 platform vars.
close_reason: Updated README: headline lists all 7 platforms, Go version corrected to 1.26.1, env-var tables now enumerate all 7 platform overrides, removed stale reference-only distinction

title: Parse .gemini/commands/*.toml files in Gemini parser
description:
docs/platforms/cross-platform-mapping.md lists Gemini slash commands as '.gemini/commands/*.toml' (TOML format with {{args}}, !{shell}, @{path} placeholders). The current internal/parser/gemini/gemini.go only parses SKILL.md under skills/ and GEMINI.md — TOML commands are silently dropped.

Add TOML command parsing that surfaces them as model.SkillTypePrompt artifacts with name=filename stem, trigger='/<name>'. Preserve TOML keys (description, prompt, etc.) in skill.Metadata so transformer can round-trip to other platforms.
acceptance_criteria: .gemini/commands/*.toml files are discovered as Type=prompt; round-trip via discover lists them; unit tests cover happy + malformed-TOML paths
close_reason: Already implemented in gemini.go:144 (parseCommandFiles). TestDiscoverGeminiTOMLCommands e2e test covers happy path. Parser returns SkillTypePrompt with TOML metadata. Implementation was added prior to this task being filed.

title: Add e2e sync round-trip tests for Pi.dev
description:
PiDevFixture exists in e2e/fixtures.go but no TestSync*PiDev* tests use it. Add round-trip coverage for:
- claude-code -> pi.dev (SKILL.md path, prompts to .pi/prompts/, instructions to AGENTS.md)
- pi.dev -> claude-code (verify SYSTEM.md / APPEND_SYSTEM.md preserve mode metadata)
- codex -> pi.dev
- discover pi.dev fixture round-trips system-prompt artifacts correctly
Verify the transformer.go:71 SYSTEM.md/APPEND_SYSTEM.md path branch with mode='append'.
acceptance_criteria: At least 3 sync tests covering pi.dev as source and target including a SYSTEM.md case; all pass
close_reason: Closed

title: Add e2e sync round-trip tests for Gemini
description:
internal/e2e/e2e_test.go has zero Gemini sync tests. Add round-trip tests covering:
- claude-code -> gemini (SKILL.md and GEMINI.md instructions)
- codex -> gemini
- gemini -> claude-code
- discover gemini fixture
Cross-check transformer's special-case in transformer.go:76 (instructions metadata routes to GEMINI.md, prompts to SKILL.md, regular skills to <name>/SKILL.md).
acceptance_criteria: At least 3 sync tests covering gemini as source and target; all pass
close_reason: Closed

title: Add e2e sync round-trip tests for Copilot
description:
internal/e2e/e2e_test.go has zero tests covering Copilot as source or target. Mirror the existing TestSyncClaudeCodeToPiAgent / TestSyncPiAgentToCursor patterns. Cover at minimum:
- claude-code -> copilot (skill, prompt, instructions)
- copilot -> claude-code (with applyTo metadata preservation)
- copilot -> codex
- discover copilot fixture round-trips name + path correctly
Add a CopilotFixture helper if missing.
acceptance_criteria: At least 3 sync tests covering copilot as source and target; all pass
close_reason: Closed

title: Reconcile portability-snapshot.yaml status with code reality
description:
docs/platforms/portability-snapshot.yaml marks copilot/gemini/pidev as 'status: reference-only', but the code provides full first-class parsers, sync source/target support, and CLI integration for all three. Pick a direction:
- (preferred) Graduate them to 'status: implemented' in the snapshot, the assessment doc, and the cross-platform-mapping support tables.
- (alternative) Gate Copilot/Gemini/PiDev behind a flag or warning and keep 'reference-only'.
After choosing, update narrative docs (portability-assessment.md, cross-platform-mapping.md, README.md) to match. The portability-check command should still pass.
acceptance_criteria: portability-check still passes; one consistent stance across snapshot, narrative docs, and CLI behavior
close_reason: Graduated copilot/gemini/pidev to 'implemented' in portability-assessment.md. Snapshot was already correct. portability-check and TestPortabilitySnapshotFreshness both pass.

title: Refresh stale 'Supported platforms' help strings in commands.go
description:
Three help strings list outdated platform sets:
- internal/cli/commands.go:254 lists 5 (missing copilot, pi-agent)
- internal/cli/commands.go:869 lists 4 (missing copilot, gemini, pi-agent)
- internal/cli/commands.go:927 lists 4 (missing copilot, gemini, pi-agent)
All three should enumerate all 7 supported platforms (claude-code, cursor, codex, pi-agent, copilot, gemini, pi.dev) or pull from a single source-of-truth helper.
acceptance_criteria: All three help strings list the same 7 platforms; if a single helper is introduced, model.AllPlatforms() is the source
close_reason: Added model.AllPlatformNames() helper; updated all 9 stale platform strings across 7 commands (discover, sync, delete, export, backup create/list/delete/verify) to reference it

title: Branch cleanup: fast-track PRs for small coherent branches
description:

title: Branch cleanup: triage feat/permission-model
description:
## Goal
Decide whether `feat/permission-model` should be split into smaller PRs or opened as one reviewable branch.

## Work
- Review the branch against `main`.
- Check whether the permissions, dependency resolution, and template work should be separated.
- Capture the recommended PR structure.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The branch has a clear recommendation: PR, split, or close.
- Any split plan is recorded clearly enough to execute later.
- The work does not duplicate existing beads tasks.
notes: Recommendation: split `feat/permission-model` instead of opening as one PR. The branch spans several unrelated tracks: permissions model/enforcement, dependency resolution and sync engine work, template/skill scaffolding, plus docs/CI/release changes. Use the existing ready beads tasks for the split pieces rather than creating duplicates: `skillsync-0lr`, `skillsync-6v2`, `skillsync-4p0`, `skillsync-8ry`, `skillsync-uo2`, `skillsync-p3j`, `skillsync-csq`, `skillsync-mle`, `skillsync-81l`, and `skillsync-18b`.
close_reason: Recommend splitting into focused PRs: permissions, dependency resolution/sync engine, template scaffolding, and docs/release/CI cleanup.

title: Branch cleanup: triage docs/sync-strategies-guide
description:
## Goal
Decide whether `docs/sync-strategies-guide` should be split, updated, or opened as a PR as-is.

## Work
- Review the branch against `main`.
- Identify any obvious split points if the branch is too large for one PR.
- Produce the smallest reviewable PR plan.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The branch has a clear next step: PR, split, or close.
- If split is recommended, the split boundaries are documented.
- Follow-up work is captured in beads if needed.
notes: Recommendation: split `docs/sync-strategies-guide` into reviewable slices rather than open it as one PR. The branch currently mixes guide/docs updates with runtime changes and test expansion. Suggested boundaries: 1) docs-only guide updates (`docs/sync-strategies.md`, `docs/commands.md`, `docs/migration.md`, `docs/quick-start.md`, related docs); 2) runtime/CLI/config changes (`internal/config`, `internal/cache`, `internal/backup`, `internal/sync`, `internal/export`, `internal/logging`, `internal/progress`, `internal/validation`); 3) security/parser/test-fixture work (`internal/security`, parser test data, e2e/integration coverage). Reuse the existing beads queue for the code slices instead of creating duplicate follow-up issues.
close_reason: Recommend splitting into docs-only, runtime/CLI/config, and security/parser/test-fixture PRs.

title: TUI: import_list.go applyFilter missing Platform and Scope from text search
description:
## Problem

import_list.go's applyFilter() at internal/ui/tui/import_list.go:559 only searches Name and Description. It omits both Platform and Scope, unlike every other skill list view.

## Expected

Text search in import list should match against Name, Platform, Scope, and Description for consistency with other views.

## Code Reference

Current import_list.go applyFilter only checks Name and Description. It should match the discover_list.go pattern that checks Name, Platform, DisplayScope, and Description.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] import_list.go applyFilter includes Platform and Scope in text search
- [ ] Tests verify all four fields are searchable
close_reason: Closed

title: TUI: sync_list.go applyFilter missing Platform from text search
description:
## Problem

sync_list.go's applyFilter() at internal/ui/tui/sync_list.go:510 searches Name, DisplayScope, and Description, but does NOT check Platform.

## Expected

Text search in sync list should match against Platform just like discover_list.go, export_list.go, and other views do.

## Code Reference

Current sync_list.go applyFilter only checks Name, DisplayScope, Description. It should also check string(s.Platform) like discover_list.go does.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] sync_list.go applyFilter includes Platform in text search
- [ ] Tests verify platform text filtering works in sync view
close_reason: Closed

title: TUI: Add discrete platform filter cycling to export, delete, and promote_demote lists
description:
## Context

After implementing the platform filter pattern in discover_list.go, the same discrete platform filter should be added to other multi-platform skill list views that support checkbox selection: export_list.go, delete_list.go, and promote_demote_list.go.

## Goal

Replicate the discover_list.go platform filter cycling UI across export, delete, and promote/demote views.

## Reference

Use the pattern established in discover_list.go (see related task). All three files share the same basic filtering structure:
- filter string + filtering bool state
- applyFilter() with text search across Name/Platform/Scope/Description
- table-based skill display

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] export_list.go supports platform filter cycling
- [ ] delete_list.go supports platform filter cycling
- [ ] promote_demote_list.go supports platform filter cycling
- [ ] All three display current platform filter in UI
- [ ] Platform filter composes with text search in all three
- [ ] Tests cover platform filter behavior
close_reason: Implemented discrete platform filter cycling across export, delete, and promote/demote TUIs with tests

title: TUI: Add discrete platform filter cycling to discover_list.go
description:
## Context

discover_list.go is the primary browsing view for skills and displays multi-platform data. It already includes platform in text search, but lacks a discrete platform filter dimension. Users who want to browse only Claude Code skills, or only Cursor skills, must type the platform name into search.

## Goal

Add a tab-cycling platform filter to discover_list.go, following the exact pattern from scope_list.go.

## Reference Implementation

scope_list.go implements:
- scopeOptions []model.SkillScope with -1 meaning "all"
- scopeIndex int tracking current selection
- tab/shift+tab keys cycling through options
- renderScopeTabs() showing active tab
- applyFilter() applying discrete filter BEFORE text filter

## Proposed Implementation

- Add platformOptions []model.Platform (including an "all" sentinel or empty string)
- Add platformIndex int
- Add left/right arrow keybindings (←/→ or h/l) to cycle platforms
- Add renderPlatformFilter() showing current platform
- Update applyFilter() to apply platform filter first, then text filter

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Left/right arrows cycle through platforms + "all"
- [ ] Current platform filter displayed in UI header/status
- [ ] Platform filter composes correctly with text search
- [ ] Esc or a dedicated key clears platform filter
- [ ] Tests cover platform filter cycling and combined filtering
close_reason: Closed

title: TUI: Add Platform column to import_list.go skill table
description:
## Context

import_list.go displays a skill selection table during import with columns: checkbox, Name, Description, Scope. It does not show the Platform column, even though imported skills have a platform.

## Goal

Add a Platform column to the import skill table so users can see which platform each skill belongs to before selecting it.

## Code Reference

- initSkillTable() at internal/ui/tui/import_list.go:513 defines columns
- skillsToRows() at internal/ui/tui/import_list.go:545 builds row data

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Platform column added between Name and Description (or appropriate position)
- [ ] Column widths adjusted to fit within reasonable terminal width
- [ ] skillsToRows includes platform value for each skill
- [ ] Tests updated to account for extra column
close_reason: Closed

title: TUI: Add platform as a filter dimension across list views
description:
## Context

The skillsync TUI has text search filtering in most list views, but platform filtering is inconsistent. Some views include platform in their text search (discover, export, dedupe, delete, promote_demote), while others omit it entirely (sync, import). No view offers platform as a discrete filter dimension (like scope_list.go's tab-cycling scope filter).

## Goal

Make platform a first-class filter dimension across all TUI list views that display multi-platform data.

## Reference Pattern

scope_list.go already implements the ideal pattern: a scopeIndex cycles through scopeOptions (-1 = "all"), with tab/shift+tab keybindings. applyFilter() applies the discrete scope filter first, then the text filter.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All skill list views include platform in text search where missing
- [ ] Key skill browsing views support discrete platform filter cycling
- [ ] Platform filter state is rendered visually (tabs or status indicator)
- [ ] Filter combinations work correctly (platform + text search together)
- [ ] Tests cover platform filter logic
close_reason: Implemented in open PR #30; the branch already adds platform-based filtering and test coverage across the affected list views.

title: Translate Codex hook events into the portability model
description:
## Goal
Document the Codex hook event model and how it maps to SkillSync's portability rules.

## Work
- Update `docs/platforms/codex.md`, `docs/platforms/cross-platform-mapping.md`, and `docs/platforms/schema.yaml`.
- List the supported Codex hook events from the official docs.
- Mark turn-scope behavior, `Stop`, and `UserPromptSubmit` semantics as portable or non-portable where appropriate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The docs show the full Codex event set used by SkillSync.
- Portable metadata and runtime-only behavior are distinguished clearly.
- The mapping leaves a clear path for later parser/serializer work.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Codex hook events are represented in the mapping layer.
2. Stop and UserPromptSubmit semantics are documented clearly.
3. The task leaves a clear path for parser or serializer updates later.
close_reason: Documented Codex hook lifecycle events and portability semantics

title: Translate Gemini hook settings and extension hooks into sync rules
description:
## Goal
Document Gemini hook settings and extension hook surfaces in the portability model.

## Work
- Update `docs/platforms/gemini.md`, `docs/platforms/cross-platform-mapping.md`, and `docs/platforms/schema.yaml`.
- Describe both workspace `settings.json` hooks and extension `hooks.json` behavior.
- Call out precedence rules and anything that must be re-authored manually.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Gemini hook surfaces are categorized by portability class.
- Settings-based intent and extension runtime behavior are clearly separated.
- Manual migration requirements are explicit in the docs.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Gemini hooks are categorized correctly in the portability model.
2. Extension and settings-based hook surfaces are differentiated.
3. The mapping makes manual re-authoring requirements explicit.
close_reason: Documented Gemini settings-vs-extension hook portability and updated the portability schema

title: Translate Claude hook metadata into portable sync data
description:
## Goal
Define how Claude hook metadata should be normalized for sync.

## Work
- Update `docs/platforms/claude.md`, `docs/platforms/cross-platform-mapping.md`, and `docs/platforms/schema.yaml`.
- Separate portable frontmatter metadata from invocation/runtime semantics.
- Document any lossy translation rules for Claude-only hook behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Claude hook fields have an explicit portable/non-portable split.
- Lossy cases are documented instead of implied.
- Runtime-only behavior remains marked as Claude-specific.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Claude hook metadata has an explicit portable/non-portable split.
2. Lossy cases are documented instead of implied.
3. The translation rules align with the repo's portability stance.
close_reason: Documented Claude hook metadata-only portability and lossy translation rules

title: Migrate and synchronize hooks across platforms
description:
## Goal
Update the cross-platform hooks model so Codex, Claude, and Gemini are described in one consistent portability framework.

## Work
- Use the linked child issues for the Codex, Gemini, and Claude-specific hook semantics.
- Keep `docs/platforms/cross-platform-mapping.md` and `docs/platforms/schema.yaml` aligned with the child work.
- Do not invent runtime behavior; document what each platform actually supports.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The hook model has one clear portability story across all supported platforms.
- Each platform's runtime-only behavior is explicitly called out.
- The child issues can be implemented independently from this epic.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Cross-platform docs explicitly describe which hook surfaces are supported by each platform.
2. Hooks are classified as portable metadata vs non-portable runtime behavior where appropriate.
3. Translation rules include Codex hook event semantics from the official OpenAI docs.
4. Follow-up implementation tasks are linked as children of this epic.
close_reason: all steps complete

title: skillsync-epic-4: Maintain Claude/Codex portability assessment
description: Keep the portability assessment, platform docs, and validation tooling aligned with actual Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Agent Skills behavior as upstream tools evolve.

title: skillsync-task-4-1: Tighten non-portable behavior coverage
description: Update docs/platforms/* and architecture docs so commands, agents, plugins, and instruction files clearly separate portable, partially portable, and non-portable semantics.
close_reason: Clarified portable, partially portable, and non-portable semantics across portability docs and architecture references.

title: skillsync-task-4-2: Create machine-readable portability snapshot
description:
## Goal
Create a structured portability snapshot that acts as the source of truth for docs and validation.

## Work
- Define the snapshot schema in `docs/platforms/schema.yaml` and/or `docs/platforms/portability-snapshot.yaml`.
- Capture artifact support, precedence, and lossy-field mappings in machine-readable form.
- Keep the snapshot stable enough for automation to diff.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The snapshot includes the supported artifact types for each platform.
- Precedence and lossiness are represented explicitly.
- The snapshot can be consumed by the freshness checker task.
close_reason: Closed

title: skillsync-task-4-3: Add freshness checker and revalidation workflow
description:
## Goal
Add a check that spots stale portability claims when upstream docs or behavior change.

## Work
- Implement a lightweight script or Go command that compares docs to the portability snapshot.
- Report mismatches clearly enough to re-run the docs update task.
- Prefer deterministic output and exit codes suitable for CI.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The checker flags obvious drift between docs and the snapshot.
- The output tells the user what needs revalidation.
- The check can be run locally and in CI.
close_reason: Closed

title: skillsync-task-3-9: Add configuration management
description:
## Goal
Add user-facing configuration management for sync and platform preferences.

## Work
- Define the config file format in YAML or JSON.
- Support default sync strategies and platform-specific options.
- Route config loading through `internal/config/`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A config file can be loaded and validated.
- Defaults are applied when config is missing or partial.
- Tests cover config parsing and one override case.

title: skillsync-task-3-10: Create integration tests
description:
## Goal
Cover the end-to-end sync flow with integration tests and fixtures.

## Work
- Add end-to-end tests under `internal/e2e/`.
- Use mock or fixture platforms instead of live tool state.
- Add golden assertions for output where formatting matters.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The main sync/discovery flow is exercised from input to output.
- Fixtures are reusable and document the scenario they represent.
- At least one test fails when a key output field changes unexpectedly.

title: skillsync-task-3-8: Implement sync command
description:
## Goal
Expose synchronization through a CLI command with dry-run support.

## Work
- Add the command and wire it into the CLI tree.
- Support a dry-run mode that shows planned changes without writing files.
- Print a concise summary of what changed or would change.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The command can run in dry-run and apply modes.
- Summary output reflects actual sync results.
- Command tests cover flags and basic success/failure cases.

title: skillsync-task-3-7: Create export functionality
description:
## Goal
Export discovered or synchronized skills into stable machine-readable and human-readable formats.

## Work
- Implement JSON, YAML, and markdown export paths in `internal/export/export.go`.
- Preserve platform metadata and source identity in exported output.
- Keep batch export deterministic.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Each supported format renders successfully in tests.
- Exported data round-trips the shared skill model without dropping required fields.
- Batch export preserves stable ordering.

title: skillsync-task-3-6: Add validation logic
description:
## Goal
Validate skill syntax and compatibility before sync or export runs.

## Work
- Add validation rules in `internal/validation/validation.go`.
- Check parsed skills against the documented skill spec and platform rules.
- Return clear errors so callers can report what failed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Invalid skill data fails validation with actionable messages.
- Validation runs before sync/export paths that depend on clean input.
- Tests cover at least one valid and one invalid skill.

title: skillsync-task-3-4: Parse Claude Code plugins
description:
## Goal
Parse skills stored inside Claude Code plugin repositories.

## Work
- Read plugin manifests and locate embedded skill definitions.
- Support git-based plugin refresh flows such as clone and pull when the repository is local to the workspace.
- Map plugin skills into the shared model without losing source identity.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Plugin repositories yield parsed skills with stable source metadata.
- The parser handles a missing or malformed manifest cleanly.
- Tests cover at least one plugin fixture and one failure case.

title: skillsync-task-3-5: Implement plugin discovery
description:
## Goal
Find installed Claude Code plugins and their skill definitions.

## Work
- Scan the documented plugin directories.
- Cache discovered plugin skill data for repeatable runs.
- Keep discovery separate from parsing so it can be tested independently.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Installed plugins are discovered from the expected locations.
- Cache behavior does not hide file changes between runs.
- Tests cover discovery with at least one plugin fixture.

title: skillsync-task-3-3: Create sync strategies
description:
## Goal
Provide explicit sync strategies so callers can choose how changes are applied.

## Work
- Implement merge, overwrite, and smart strategy selection in `internal/sync/strategy.go`.
- Make strategy selection available from CLI flags or config.
- Keep strategy behavior deterministic and easy to test.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Each strategy has a clear behavior description in code or tests.
- Strategy selection is wired into the sync path.
- Tests distinguish merge, overwrite, and smart behavior.

title: skillsync-task-3-1: Implement synchronization engine
description:
## Goal
Implement the core synchronization engine that moves skills between platforms through the shared model.

## Work
- Build the engine in `internal/sync/sync.go` or the existing sync package layout.
- Support bidirectional sync by comparing source, destination, and portable metadata.
- Emit progress and logging that callers can surface in CLI or tests.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The engine can synchronize one skill set between two platforms in tests.
- The sync path returns structured results instead of ad hoc logging only.
- Unit tests cover the happy path and at least one failure path.

title: skillsync-task-3-2: Add conflict resolution
description:
## Goal
Resolve divergent skill definitions safely when both sides changed.

## Work
- Implement the conflict logic in `internal/sync/conflict.go` or the existing sync conflict layer.
- Use a three-way merge where possible.
- Prompt the user only in interactive mode; keep non-interactive mode deterministic.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Conflicts are detected reliably when source and destination diverge.
- Interactive resolution path is covered by tests or harnesses.
- Non-interactive behavior has a documented fallback.

title: skillsync-task-2-8: Implement discovery command
description:
## Goal
Add a CLI command that lists discovered skills across platforms.

## Work
- Wire the command into the CLI tree.
- Support JSON, YAML, and table output.
- Support filtering by platform and skill type.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The command runs end-to-end against the shared discovery layer.
- Output formats are deterministic and tested.
- Filters narrow the result set without changing the underlying discovery logic.
close_reason: Closed

title: skillsync-task-2-7: Add platform detection
description:
## Goal
Detect installed and configured platforms automatically.

- Or suppress the warning if the dir is inside a worktree that the user trusts (probably out of scope)
